case_slice: Two concurrent passive branch activations after operated-branch failures

parent.accepted_scope: two initially operated B/A, one C standby, NBREQ=NBOP=2, TSWOV=0.5h; B failure starts C activation and A fails later

prior_diagnostic.finding: Both arms completed two nonoverlapping switches. At B failure h8.62763 the log schedules next random failure h16.7498; the four-hour B→C switch ends h12.6276, then A failure is rescheduled to h15.0942. The short arm A failure is h11.5942. This nine-hour probe intentionally crosses the initially logged h16.7498 candidate. The v1.0.0 diagnostic is not published as overlap.

model.rbd: G05-PASSIVE, NBREQ=NBOP=2, ONLM=N; B/A priority1/2 initially operated, C/D priority3/4 passive and nonfailing
model.failure_modes: unchanged FM-POS-B 600000 and FM-POS-A 300000 per million operating hours; C/D no configured mode
model.repair: unchanged B/A half-hour direct system CM after return

source_delta: From accepted three-branch two-operated parent, add POS-D and one TEACH-LRU-01 on D to MaterielPosition/MaterielStructure/MaterielOperationalModes/RBDParallelStructure, and change descriptive text to four branches. The short arm keeps TSWOV=0.5. The long arm differs from the short arm only in RBDParallel.TSWOV 0.5→9.0 h and ProblemDescription.PDESC. This pair isolates switch-duration overlap within the same four-branch topology.
manual_basis: Installed SIMLOX 2017 manual pp197–200 and 455–458 define passive parallel operation, NBREQ/NBOP counting, PRIO and TSWOV. The direct G05.var02 parent is accepted native evidence for two initially operated branches and one activation.

pre_run_hypotheses.accepted_parent: With three branches and TSWOV0.5, B fails h8.62763, B→C completes h9.12763, and A fails h11.5942. These are observations, not asserted unchanged draws in the new four-branch pair.
pre_run_hypotheses.short_control: If draws remain stable, B→C finishes before A fails, then A→D finishes 0.5 h later; the two activation intervals do not overlap.
pre_run_hypotheses.long_overlap: The prior diagnostic log initially scheduled a next failure at h16.7498 when B→C began h8.62763. A nine-hour B→C switch would finish near h17.62763, so that candidate event lies inside activation. If it fires on operated A during activation and a spare D is selected, A→D starts before B→C completes. The raw intervals and report bins decide.
pre_run_hypotheses.alternatives: The engine may suspend or reschedule A's failure during B→C activation, as the four-hour run rescheduled it after B→C finished. A nine-hour arm may therefore still have no overlap or a different mission outcome. Preserve the raw trace and do not preaccept a predicted result.
pre_run_hypotheses.observability: Positive overlap requires two raw switch-start events with distinct destination branches, first switch still pending at second start, both completion events, identified operated-branch faults, and report-bin reconciliation. Two faults or a long aggregate NSYSW alone are insufficient.

acceptance_gates: Frozen parent and paired source hashes, exact parent-to-short and short-to-long deltas, installed source hashes
Two separate session-0 SSH runs under one host-wide native mutex, unique run directories, preserved GUI PID 13340
Each arm imports/exports/calculates/reports with exact authored-row roundtrip and zero converter errors
Actual switch and failure intervals, mission outcome, 72-bin System/Stock ledgers reconciled by author and independent read-only reviewer
Raw invocation, logs, models, reports and closures SHA-256 sealed for both runs
limits: One fixed seed and repetition, one two-operated four-branch passive RBD, one short and one nine-hour TSWOV pair.
The short-to-long pair isolates TSWOV within four branches; adding D relative to the three-branch parent is a necessary capacity change and may alter random scheduling.
If two overlapping native switch intervals are not observed, retain the run as a diagnostic probe and do not publish G05.var05.
Unavailable preferred standby G05.var04, nested propagation G05.var06 beyond its own published scope, GUI view and cross-engine parity are separate.
